title: Hiring funnel heuristics and role-fit heatmap
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for two related needs: (1) concise heuristics to standardize funnel decisions across fast-hiring roles, and (2) a lightweight role-fit heatmap to help hiring panels converge faster on evidence-based offers.

Context / problem statement:
- We are seeing divergence between hiring managers and interview panels on what "must-have" vs "nice-to-have" skills look like for cross-functional IC roles.
- Interview score distributions are noisy (mode near "3" with a lot of midline justifications).
- Onboarding handoff is often late because role-fit signals are not surfaced early (lack of clear heatmap + explicit risks).

High-level heuristics (short):
1) Pre-screen threshold: resume + takehome "sanity check" should filter out roles with < 60% match on core signals (years + demonstrable ownership + repo or product sample). If < 60% then reject or reassign to a lower band.
2) Evidence-first interviewing: each behavioral/technical question must map to 1–2 scorecard signals. If an interviewer can't point to a specific evidence item for a score >=4, default to a 3 and surface for calibration.
3) Risk-weighted offers: every candidate with >2 red flags in the heatmap must have hiring manager sign-off and a documented mitigation plan in the offer doc.
4) Fast-path vs Slow-path: define top-of-funnel signals that allow a candidate to take the "fast-path": (open source contribution, shipped feature, prior infra/scale experience). Fast-path shortens the loop to 2 onsite rounds.

Scorecard design (practical guidance):
- Keep 5 axes max per role: Core product skills, System level/scale, Ownership + shipping, Collaboration/communication, Learning curve/adjacent skills.
- Use 1–5 scale with clear anchors:
  1 = No evidence / contradicts claim
  2 = Limited evidence; needs heavy coaching
  3 = Competent for immediate task with manager support
  4 = Strong; can lead small projects
  5 = Distinguished; can mentor/drive cross-team outcomes
- Mandatory comments: any 4 or 5 must include the concrete evidence sentence ("Built X that did Y for Z users; link: ...").
- Red flags taxonomy (checkbox-style): ethics/compliance incident, persistently poor communication, mismatch of compensation expectation vs role band, lack of core technical baseline.

Role-fit heatmap (how to build quickly in interview notes):
- Columns = candidate signals (experience slice, sample work, takehome, onsite round 1, onsite round 2)
- Rows = scorecard axes from above
- Cells = short token: + (evidence supports), ~ (inconclusive), - (contra).
- At panel debrief, produce a 1-row summary: overall fit band (green/amber/red), top 3 evidence bullets, top 2 risks + mitigations.

Running a calibration session (30–45m template):
- 5m: framing (why we need this consistency)
- 10m: show 3 anonymized candidate sheets with divergent scores (pick real recent examples)
- 10m: small-group re-score (2 people per group)
- 10m: highlight where anchors differ; update anchors and hotfix wording on the scorecard
- 5m: agree on immediate actions (who updates which job template, who notifies hiring manager)

Panel interviewer cheat sheet (1-pager to paste in invite):
- Role band and non-negotiables
- One-sentence hiring manager success metric (what 90 days looks like)
- 3 suggested questions mapped to score axes (sends them to panel so they don't re-invent)
- Guidance: call out missing evidence in comments, and use the heatmap tokens during debrief.

Onboarding handoff checklist (min viable, to attach to offer acceptance):
- Day 0: access list (low-privilege first: corp email, payroll, basic SSO) — status: assigned to HR ops
- Day 1–7: role immersion plan + first ticket to own (manager to assign), buddy pairing scheduled, kickoff doc sent
- Week 2: 90-day goals draft (manager + candidate) + security briefing complete
- Week 4: first feedback pulse (people ops + manager)
- Week 8: cross-team intro and small project allocation
- Week 12: probation review; convert to performance plan or close gaps

How the heatmap informs onboarding priorities:
- If heatmap shows weak system-level/scale evidence: prioritize paired shadowing and a logging/observability ticket in first 30 days.
- If collaboration axis is ~ or -: assign explicit communication expectations (meeting cadence, PR review SLAs) and a mentorship pairing.

Examples / micro-templates (paste into interview notes quickly):
- Evidence sentence: "Led infra migration for payments; reduced latency by 45% at 100k TPS; link: github.com/org/repo/PR#123"
- Risk + mitigation: "Limited infra exposure -> mitigation: 6-week buddy program + dedicated infra project with senior mentor"

Open questions / trade offs (notes):
- Should we enforce take-homes for all mid-senior ICs? Pros: higher signal. Cons: drops conversion and candidate diversity. Suggest: make takehome optional but required for fast-path bypass.
- How prescriptive should managers be about the 5 axes? For cross-pool hiring we recommend standard axes, with role-specific optional sub-axes.

Immediate action items (owner - ETA):
- Maya: draft main scorecard template and publish to Confluence (ETA 2025-10-05)
- Diego: run calibration session for Platform + Serving hires (ETA 2025-10-12)
- Aisha: update interview invite template to include the 1-pager cheat sheet (ETA 2025-10-07)

Notes to self / working fragments:
- Consider a lightweight Google Sheet generator where interviewers tick +/~/- and it renders the heatmap summary row automatically. Might be a 2-day eng partner task.
- Capture 4 anonymized candidate notes to use as calibration examples; ask hiring managers for permission.

Appendix (links for reference):
- Existing scorecards: confluence:HR-Scorecards-2024 (use as starting point)
- Candidate flow metrics dashboard: metabase: hiring-funnel-velocity

This is rough; intended to be a living doc. Use in current monthly hiring guild retro and refine anchors over Q4.
